# thoughtfeel

> thoughtfeel is a sense for concepts. It lets you take in a concept and its properties all at once, the way vision lets you take in what’s in front of you.

Just as people can imagine in pictures or in sounds, people with thoughtfeel can imagine in concepts. Like vision and hearing, it differs from person to person, and it most likely varies the way the mind’s eye does. Based on studies of unsymbolized thinking, about 73% of people have some of it, some have none, and among those who have it, it ranges from faint to vivid. (Source: Russell Hurlburt’s study of inner experience, Heavey & Hurlburt, 2008, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.concog.2007.12.006. 22 of 30 people had unsymbolized thinking at least once: a specific thought that comes without words or pictures.)

thoughtfeel.net is a practical guide to harnessing that ability to learn faster and remember more, by Ted Shachtman, who named the sense thoughtfeel. The name is written as one lowercase word, as on the YouTube channel (youtube.com/@ThoughtFeelGuide).

What thoughtfeel is not:

- Not your mind’s eye or inner voice. Pictures and words can come along with a thought, but thoughtfeel works without them.
- Not an emotion. The economy and justice feel different from each other, but neither one feels happy or sad.
- Not the feeling of knowing. Everyone knows what they’re thinking. thoughtfeel gives the thought itself detail you can notice, the way a picture has detail.
- Not a technique. thoughtfeel is the sense. The lessons teach techniques that use it, the way the memory palace uses the mind’s eye.

## The definition

- [What is thoughtfeel?](https://thoughtfeel.net/what-is-thoughtfeel/): the definition, with examples, and what thoughtfeel is not

## Do you have it?

- [The one-question quiz](https://thoughtfeel.net/quiz/): the four ways to think about your best friend (a picture, their voice, just knowing, a concept bubble); if you can get a sense of the fourth, you have thoughtfeel

## Lessons

- [Start here: Why Visual Analogies Fail for Complex Concepts (and What Would Work Instead)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g3Z8VnARbQg)
- [How to Learn Anything Complicated by Building a Concept Story](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dV8fNY311W4): the full walkthrough; [the full texts](https://thoughtfeel.net/texts/)

- [How to Memorize Any List by Imagining in Concepts](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mFIThyF5Y0E)
- [How to Memorize Long Numbers by Imagining in Concepts](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DpkQsCGBMIE)
- [How to Memorize Vocabulary by Imagining in Concepts](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VDHt3z8Babo); try it on [ten Spanish words](https://thoughtfeel.net/words/)
